scope: Non-default asset on purpose, so the default inspection road is untouched. One launch each, derived cache warmed for both configurations, no leftover gz or rviz2 process before either, mesh change only with the display textures unchanged. Per-process RSS sampled every 2 s; no VRAM counter in this harness.

delta.superseded_by: repeat; the single-run -17.3 s was optimistic

optix_input_unchanged.basis: compared against manifest.json.before_display_mesh; OptiX LoadScene reads assets[*].mesh

code_path_audit.optix_reads: gz_linescan.cpp:1008 OptixScene(rays, scenePath_, robotPath_, ptxPath_, ...); scenePath_ is the manifest and optix/scene_io.h LoadScene walks assets[*].mesh
code_path_audit.optix_never_touches_ogre2: no reference to gz rendering anywhere under src/agv_linescan/src/optix/; render_ appears six times in the plugin, all inside backend_=="render" branches
code_path_audit.render_backend_excluded: check_display_mesh_backend refuses to launch it on a scene declaring display_mesh
code_path_audit.lidar_feedback_ruled_out: lidar returns do change, but /lidar/*/points is bridged GZ to ROS only and nothing in the workspace subscribes; localisation uses GNSS, IMU and wheel odometry
code_path_audit.physics_unaffected: the world holds exactly one collision element, the heightmap; terrain models have none
code_path_audit.materials_separate: OptiX uses the six ground_material .raw payloads; the display PNGs are GZ-only and were not touched by this change
code_path_audit.boundary: the conclusion rests on the launch-time exclusion. Bypassing sim.launch.py and running the render backend on this road would image the light mesh.
code_path_audit.why_not_pixels: a mission-level pixel comparison is unavailable here; input identity is the stronger claim, since identical pixels would only be a consequence of it

reading: Geometry, not texture, was the dominant term: the raw vertex data fell by 731 MB yet each process fell by about 3.5 GiB, so the Ogre2 footprint is several times the source data. The 1.28 and 0.73 GiB that remain are mostly the still-full-size display textures.
limits: one run per configuration, so the time figure deserves repeats; the memory difference is far outside any run-to-run variation seen here
this asset carries no physics heightmap, so its terrain models still have collision elements; the default road does not
GZ and RViz windows were not inspected by eye in this run
lidar returns were not compared; the display mesh drops joints up to 3 mm deep

repeat.note: second run of each configuration on the non-default asset

default_road.reading: all four missions passed with ESTIMATED_COMPLETE and ACQUIRED/HOLD at an unchanged RTF. This metric carries about 10 s of run-to-run spread in both groups, so its worst case is weak; the memory-plateau measurement on the non-default asset is the better controlled one.

fidelity_measured.method: the display surface interpolated at every optical vertex, against the optical height
fidelity_measured.correction: an earlier note said the display surface is point-for-point identical outside the defects. That holds only at vertices the two meshes share. The display mesh is a 20 cm grid and interpolates linearly between its nodes, so against the exact heightfield it is up to 0.20 mm out, about a tenth of the 2 mm relief amplitude.
